country.name: Andorra
country.description: Andorra is a tiny Pyrenean principality between France and Spain with a single unified ski pass (Andorra Pass) covering Grandvalira (Soldeu/El Tarter/Pas de la Casa/Grau Roig), Pal Arinsal, and Ordino Arcalís — a combined 308 km of pistes, 116 lifts, and the longest ski season in the Pyrenees. Grandvalira Resorts sold 2.32 million ski days in 2025/26 (+4% YoY). Andorra is positioned as the best-value ski destination in Europe — lift passes, accommodation, and food are significantly cheaper than the Alps. 53% of visitors are Spanish, 15% British/Irish (growing 3% YoY), with increasing US visitors via Ikon Pass reciprocity.

industry_overview.world_rank_by_skier_days: Top 5 in sales ranking globally (Grandvalira Resorts claims top 5 in ski day sales among single ski groups)
industry_overview.annual_skier_visits: ~2.5 million ski days sold per season
industry_overview.total_ski_areas: 3 (Grandvalira, Pal Arinsal, Ordino Arcalís — under single Andorra Pass)

top_markets.uk_ireland: 15% of total (21% at Pal Arinsal, growing 3% YoY)
top_markets.us_growth: Increasing — Ikon Pass reciprocity with Grandvalira Resorts

industry_overview.source_figures: Grandvalira Resorts official season close press release 2026; Grandvalira corporate site

currency.name: Euro
currency.notes: Andorra uses the Euro despite not being an EU member. It is a tax haven — no VAT (sales tax). This means shopping (electronics, alcohol, tobacco, perfume, ski gear) is up to 30-40% cheaper than in France or Spain. British skiers routinely stock up on alcohol, tobacco, and electronics. Duty-free allowances still apply when returning to EU countries. Cash widely used but card accepted in most places.

language.street_signs: Catalan (first language), with Spanish, French, English on tourist signage
language.english_in_resorts: Very good — all major resorts have English-speaking staff at ticket offices, ski schools, rental shops, and hotels. British and Irish are the second-largest market (15% of visitors).

power_plugs.type: Type G (UK-style 3-pin rectangular) — Andorra uses British standard plugs
power_plugs.adapter_needed: NO if coming from UK — same as UK plug. YES if coming from continental Europe (US, France, Germany, etc.) — they need a UK adapter.
power_plugs.notes: Andorra is one of very few non-Commonwealth countries using British-style sockets. A rare convenience for UK skiers.

practical_info_for_skiers.time_zone: CET (UTC+1) winter; CEST (UTC+2) summer. Same as France and Spain. 1 hour ahead of UK.

driving_from_uk.calais_to_andorra: ~10-11 hours. Route: Calais-Reims-Dijon-Lyon-Orange-Perpignan then up the RN22/E9 into Andorra. Alternatively Calais-Bordeaux-Toulouse (longer).
driving_from_uk.driving_from_barcelona: ~2.5 hours (200 km north via C-16/E9). Park at the border (Andorra has limited parking — free parking at Grandvalira's car parks but fills fast in peak weeks).
driving_from_uk.driving_from_toulouse: ~2 hours via A61 to Foix then RN20/E9.
driving_from_uk.tolls: French autoroutes from Calais to Perpignan ~€70-85 one-way. Spanish highways on return ~€10-15. No tolls in Andorra itself.
driving_from_uk.fuel: Andorra has significantly cheaper fuel than France or Spain (tax haven). Fill up in Andorra before driving back. Expect €1.15-1.25/litre vs €1.60-1.80 in France.

winter_driving_law.legal_requirement: Winter tyres or chains mandatory when weather conditions require (Andorran law mirrors French/Spanish mountain driving rules).
winter_driving_law.enforcement: Police checks on mountain access roads (RN22/E9 into Andorra). Fines for inadequate winter equipment. Chains required on the steep approach to Pas de la Casa (Andorra's border with France at 2,400m).

speed_limits.mountain_roads: 60 km/h (often reduced in snow — follow variable signs)
speed_limits.fines: Speeding fines from €60-600 depending on excess. Speed cameras on the main routes. Andorran police enforce strictly but fairly.

ev_charging.availability: Good in the main axes (Andorra la Vella and resort car parks). Limited in remote areas. Most hotels now have destination chargers.

ski_insurance.andorran_system: No single equivalent of France's Carré Neige. Rescue and medical costs are charged and claimed back from travel insurance.
ski_insurance.rescue_costs: Ski patrol rescue €100-500 for on-piste. Helicopter evacuation €1,000-3,000+. Travel insurance with winter sports cover is essential.
ski_insurance.rega_note: REGA does not cover Andorra (it's Swiss only).
ski_insurance.travel_insurance: Essential. UK travel insurance with European winter sports cover. Most UK policies cover Andorra under 'Europe' cover.

emergency_services.european_emergency: 112 (works across Andorra. Free from any phone. English-speaking operators available.)

andorran_numbers.mountain_rescue: 112 (activates Andorran mountain rescue — Grup de Rescat de Muntanya)

mountain_rescue.grup_de_rescat: Andorran Mountain Rescue Group — professional team. Activated via 112.
mountain_rescue.resort_patrol: Each resort has its own piste patrol (Pistaires) — first responders for on-piste incidents.
mountain_rescue.cost: Rescue incurs a charge. Claimable from travel insurance.

ski_customs_and_regulations.helmet_law: Not legally required for adults or children. Strongly recommended. Some ski schools require them for children.
ski_customs_and_regulations.duty_free_shopping: Andorra is a duty-free haven. No VAT. Electronics, alcohol, tobacco, perfume, and ski gear significantly cheaper than EU. Duty-free allowances apply when returning to France or Spain: 4 litres of spirits, 16 litres of beer, €430 value on other goods. Border customs checks can occur.
ski_customs_and_regulations.ikon_pass: Grandvalira Resorts is on the Ikon Pass. US/Ikon pass holders get discounted access — a significant draw for North American visitors.

country.price_positioning_vs_peers: Andorra is the best-value ski destination in Europe for UK skiers. A 6-day lift pass in 2025/26: ~€270-310 total (€45-52/day, Andorra Pass). Cheaper than France (€354/6d, €59/day), Italy (€306/6d, €51/day), Austria (€402/6d, €67/day), and 60% cheaper than Switzerland. Accommodation is 30-50% cheaper than equivalent French Alpine resorts. Mountain restaurant lunch: €12-18 vs €22-35 in France. No VAT = shopping is 20-23% cheaper for everything from ski gear to electronics. The value comes with trade-offs: lower altitude (highest pistes at 2,640m Pas de la Casa), smaller total terrain (308km vs 600km in 3 Vallées), and more weather-dependent early/late season. But for budget-conscious groups, families, and intermediate skiers, Andorra offers the best bang-for-buck in Europe.
country.season_general: Early December to mid-April (Grandvalira Resorts claims the longest season in the Pyrenees — 2025/26 ran 134 days, 8 Dec–20 Apr). Snowmaking on 66% of terrain. November opening possible in good snow years. April skiing can be variable — lower slopes suffer but upper Pas de la Casa sector often holds snow until late April.
